test.title: Mini-test · Car-free city centres
textTitles: Is it time to close city centres to cars?

texts.title: Is it time to close city centres to cars?

paragraphs.text: Several European cities have closed parts of their centres to private cars, and the idea is now being discussed in many others. As someone who has lived in a car-free district for three years, I am generally in favour, although I do not think a complete ban suits every town.

The benefits I have noticed are real. The air feels cleaner, the streets are quieter, and children play outside in places that were once too dangerous. Local cafés have put tables on the pavement, and on summer evenings the neighbourhood is busier than it ever was when cars were allowed.

Shopkeepers were the strongest opponents of the plan. They feared that customers who could no longer park outside would go elsewhere. For some businesses, especially those selling heavy goods such as furniture, this fear was justified, and a few have moved away. Most, however, have kept their customers.

A ban only works if people have good alternatives. Our district is served by frequent trams, and there are cycle lanes on every main road. In a small town with one bus an hour, closing the centre to cars would simply cut residents off from shops and services.

Elderly and disabled residents deserve particular attention. Taxis and delivery vans are still permitted in our area at certain times, and I believe this flexibility is essential. A policy that makes life easier for the young and fit while trapping others at home cannot be called a success.

items.prompt: The writer supports closing the centre to cars in every town.
The writer says he has lived in a car-free area.
The writer feels that the air in the district has become cleaner.
The writer thinks the neighbourhood is less lively than before the change.
The writer accepts that the shopkeepers’ fears were justified for some businesses.
The writer thinks the council should pay compensation to businesses that moved away.
The writer claims that most businesses lost customers after the change.
The writer believes a ban needs good public transport to succeed.
The writer considers trams to be a better choice than buses for any town.
The writer thinks allowing taxis in at certain times is unnecessary.

Write YES if the statement agrees with the views of the writer, NO if the statement contradicts the views of the writer, or NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
